statement:
Define `track_indicator(initial_ids, selected_index, operations)`.

The state is an ordered tab strip whose tabs have distinct signed 64-bit integer identifiers. At most one tab is selected; its zero-based position is the indicator index.

`initial_ids` is the initial order. If it is empty, `selected_index` is `-1`. Otherwise, `0 <= selected_index < len(initial_ids)`, and that position is initially selected.

Each element of `operations` is one of:

* `("insert", p, ids)`: `ids` is a nonempty sequence of identifiers that have never appeared before, even as removed tabs. Insert them in their given order immediately before position `p`, where `0 <= p <= current_length`. An existing selection remains attached to the same identifier. If the strip was empty, the first inserted identifier becomes selected.
* `("remove", ids)`: `ids` is a nonempty sequence of pairwise distinct identifiers, all currently present. Remove them simultaneously. If the selected identifier survives, it remains selected. Otherwise, use the order immediately before this operation and disregard every removed tab other than the selected tab: select the first surviving tab to its right; if none exists, select the last surviving tab to its left; if none survives, leave the strip unselected.
* `("reverse", left, right)`: reverse the order of all tabs at positions from `left` through `right - 1`, where `0 <= left < right <= current_length`. Selection remains attached to the same identifier.

After every operation, append the current indicator index to the result, or `-1` if no tab is selected. Return the resulting list.

All identifiers in `initial_ids` are distinct. There are at most 200,000 operations. The total number of identifiers in `initial_ids` and all `insert` operations is at most 300,000. The total number of identifiers listed by all `remove` operations is at most 300,000. Reversed ranges have no bound on their combined length.

The implementation must be deterministic, use only the Python standard library, perform no input/output, and must not modify the supplied sequences.
